title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

The corrective action that has been apparent in mid- and small-cap land has now started to show up in the large caps as well. So far, this pullback still fits the profile of a normal and healthy breather after a strong push off the lows. Importantly, the major indices remain decisively above their 20- and 50-day moving averages, keeping the intermediate-term uptrend intact. That said, this is the point in the cycle where the character of the tape matters. A short, contained pullback is constructive. What would change the posture is meaningful violation of key moving averages or a breakdown in structure—specifically, a shift toward lower highs and lower lows. Those are the signals that the correction is no longer just digestion.

The sector picture remains rotational and uneven. Technology, which has clearly been the leadership engine, is finally taking a breather. That’s not only normal—it’s arguably necessary to reset extension and allow higher-quality setups to form. Most other sectors remain in digestion mode as well, pulling back or chopping sideways and failing to show the same degree of sponsorship and momentum that Tech carried earlier. Until broader participation returns, this remains a market where the index-level trend may still look fine, but opportunities remain more selective and stock-specific.

Internals reflect this corrective phase. Breadth and momentum have continued to cool off—expected after a sharp advance—but the softening has been more pronounced outside of Technology. Several areas, including Materials, Consumer, Healthcare, and Financials, have seen internal readings weaken as new highs contract and downside pressure increases. This suggests demand is thinning in the average stock, which is why breakouts may become less reliable until participation improves. If the market is going to sustain a durable advance, the key development to watch next is internal re-broadening: new highs stabilizing and expanding again, new lows staying contained, and more sectors regaining positive momentum—not just Tech.

1) Trend & Market Structure

The pullback is now broadening into large caps, but so far it still looks like a normal digestion phase after a strong run. The key fact is that indices remain above the 20/50-day moving averages, keeping the intermediate trend constructive.

Tactical guidance

  • Stay in constructive-but-selective offense: 50–65% of normal risk.

  • Treat this as a buyable reset only if pullbacks remain contained above the 20-day and price structure holds.

  • Watch for a character change:

    • Caution triggers: multiple indices lose the 20-day on volume, or structure shifts to lower highs/lower lows.

    • If that happens, reduce exposure toward 30–45% quickly.

2) Breadth & Momentum (Primary Throttle)

Internals are softening with the pullback, and that reduces breakout reliability. This is expected, but it’s also the key factor that determines whether this stays a controlled reset or becomes something heavier.

Tactical guidance

  • Lower expectations for broad follow-through; trade fewer, higher-quality setups.

  • Maintain exposure if:

    • new lows remain contained, and

    • internals stabilize after the pullback.

  • Press exposure only if internals re-broaden:

    • new highs expand for multiple sessions, and

    • downside pressure fades across more sectors.

3) Sector Focus & Rotation

Tech is still the leadership engine, but it’s finally taking a needed breather. Most other sectors remain in digestion mode, and several (Materials, Consumer, Healthcare, Financials) are showing weaker internal tone.

Tactical guidance

  • Keep Tech as a primary focus, but concentrate on pullback entries and basing setups.

  • In non-Tech sectors, a tight structure is required near support before participating.

  • Avoid broad exposure in sectors where internals are turning negative until they stabilize and RS improves.

4) Stock Selection & Entries

This is a market where edge comes from tight patterns near support, not extended entries.

Prioritize

  • Tech leaders forming tight bases or pulling back cleanly to the 10/20-day.

  • Best-of-breed names in other sectors only if they hold structure and show RS improvement.

  • Controlled pullbacks with clear invalidation (swing low / 20-day).

Avoid

  • Chasing strength after multiple up days.

  • Loose, wide-range patterns.

  • Breakouts in groups with deteriorating internals.

5) Trade Management & Risk Controls

As the market digests, tighten management slightly.

  • Position size: ½–¾ normal (full size only on A+ setups).

  • Stops: below swing low / base low / 20-day (depending on pattern).

  • Take partial profits (25–50%) if a name pops quickly or gets extended.

  • Trail remainder with 10-day (fast leaders) or 20-day (slower).

If a position stalls or loses structure during the pullback, cut it—don’t let a digestion turn into a drawdown.

6) Exposure Controls & Scenarios

Base case (now): healthy pullback

  • Exposure: 50–65%

  • Cash: 20–35% to take advantage of new bases forming

Bullish continuation

  • Indices hold 20-day + internals re-broaden + leaders tighten and break higher
    → scale toward 65–80% selectively.

Character change / deeper correction

  • Loss of 20-day across multiple indices + new lows expand + structure deteriorates
    → reduce to 30–45%, tighten stops, raise cash.

Bottom Line

This is still a normal and healthy breather within an uptrend—for now. The market remains above key intermediate-term support, but internals are soft and participation is thinning outside of Tech. Stay selectively engaged, focus on tight pullback/basing setups near the 10/20-day, and be ready to de-risk quickly if the market loses the 20-day or shifts into lower-low/lower-high behavior. tighten up.
